title: Agni
context: Opening hymn of the Rigveda, addressed to Agni.

title: Indra and Vṛtra
context: A hymn narrating Indra’s slaying of Vṛtra and the release of the waters.

title: Indra, who slew the dragon
context: A hymn identifying Indra by deeds, including the slaying of the dragon and the freeing of rivers.

title: Viśvāmitra and the Rivers
context: A dialogue hymn: a seer asks the Vipāś and Śutudrī to lower themselves for a crossing.

title: Varuṇa and release from bonds
context: A prayer to Varuṇa for knowledge, mercy, and release.

title: Uṣas, the Dawn
context: A dawn hymn joining awakening and radiance with the measure of mortal days.

title: Rudra
context: A careful praise of fierce Rudra that asks for protection and healing remedies.

title: Uṣas
context: Dawn reveals the world and wakes its inhabitants.

title: Varuṇa and confession
context: The poet asks what offence has angered Varuṇa and seeks release.

title: The Frog Hymn
context: Frogs call after the rains and are compared with ritual reciters.

title: We have drunk Soma
context: A hymn of Soma's exhilaration and promise.

title: Soma Pavamāna
context: Soma is praised while flowing and being purified.

title: Soma and the deathless realm
context: A hymn asking Soma to place the singer in realms of light and immortality.

title: The Gambler's Lament
context: A first-person poem about dice, compulsion, estrangement, and return to work.

title: Vāc Sūkta
context: A first-person hymn in which Vāc declares her reach among gods and worlds.

title: Yama and Yamī
context: A dialogue concerning desire, kinship, and cosmic order.

title: The funeral hymn
context: A hymn of the funeral: Yama, the path of the departed, and the fathers.

title: Agni and the body of the dead
context: A closely related funeral hymn addressing Agni and the burning of the body.

title: Burial and the living
context: A closely related funeral hymn: death is sent away, and the living are told to turn back.

title: The marriage hymn
context: The wedding of Sūryā, later recited in marriage ritual. The later ritual use is not the same as the hymn’s own scene.

title: Puruṣa Sūkta
context: A cosmogonic hymn: Puruṣa is offered, and the world and social orders are said to arise from the parts.

title: Purūravas and Urvaśī
context: A dialogue hymn: a mortal calls after an Apsaras at daybreak.

title: Sarama and the Paṇis
context: A dialogue hymn: Sarama, sent toward the Paṇis, demands the hidden cows.

title: Hiraṇyagarbha
context: A hymn of the golden embryo, with a refrain asking to which god the offering belongs.

title: Nāsadīya Sūkta
context: Creation / cosmology. The hymn asks what there was, and who could know.
